claims.claim: Authority and holder checks return typed ok:False for RPC errors and bad bodies (RpcError and DataStale), and for malformed payloads (AttributeError, KeyError, TypeError, ValueError); any other exception propagates. Source: authorities.py, holders.py.
The existing authority and holder characterization outputs are unchanged on the success and not-found paths.

The pump event decoder round-trips all five event types, ignores trailing bytes, and raises EventDecodeError on every truncation and on truncated base64 program data; unknown discriminators raise UnknownEventError (a subclass).

The four pinned discriminators (TradeEvent, CreateEvent, CompleteEvent, CompletePumpAmmMigrationEvent) equal sha256('event:<Name>')[:8] and match the research pins; PostCompleteBuyEvent discriminator 6fb06d8b316cd5fb is derived by the same rule and is not pinned in the research.
Money fields are integer base units; the decoder uses no float money. Base58 pubkeys are rendered by a local encoder pinned to two known byte strings.
Trading smoke pin and smoke-10m events.hash are unchanged (b69c29593954129b52a8c9ab1cad390441b7b356dd482b8c7a4345bea55ad32d).

Behaviour change for callers: RpcError and DataStale now report their own redacted message (for example 'rpc bad body method=... endpoints=N') instead of the generic 'authority check failed' / 'holder check failed'. Non-RPC, non-malformed exceptions now propagate to the caller instead of returning ok:false.

Pump decoder layouts are not in the repo. TradeEvent (through mayhem_mode, including ix_name before mayhem_mode), CreateEvent (stops before token_program and is_mayhem_mode, which are trailing bytes and ignored), CompleteEvent, CompletePumpAmmMigrationEvent and PostCompleteBuyEvent follow the research spec and the public pump IDL as recalled; they are unverified against chain.
